benefit: If a future system is independently validated, potentially faster identification of cases for review; no direct benefit is claimed for the synthetic exercise.
harm: A missed case, unnecessary scrutiny, stigma, unequal prioritization, privacy intrusion, or no practical avenue to correct an error.
participation: No consultation occurred in this exercise. Before any real use, include affected people in co-design, understandable notice, testing, and an independent correction/appeal route.

benefit: A ranked queue may help organize workload if validated and used only as a secondary aid.
harm: Automation bias, excess false-positive workload, overlooked cases, unclear accountability, or pressure to treat a score as a decision.
participation: Train on limits and override; pilot only in a safe non-operational setting; capture reasons and disagreements; include reviewers in monitoring and incident exercises.

benefit: A documented process may support accountable allocation of human review if a legitimate need is established.
harm: Legal, service, reputational, and human-rights consequences from invalid or discriminatory use, weak oversight, or scope creep.
participation: Name an accountable owner; require legal/privacy review, affected-party participation, approval gates, monitoring, appeal and suspension authority before any real deployment.

benefit: Reproducible evidence can reveal model limitations and support safer analysis.
harm: Data quality or leakage errors, unstable subgroup estimates, misleading metrics, and responsibility for unsupported claims.
participation: Document data provenance and code; validate schemas and temporal split; report subgroup/intersectional uncertainty; independently review changes and incidents.
